chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to me; Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim Majilawayh narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Qurashi from Ubayd ibn Yahya al-Thawri from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) visited us one day, so we presented food to him. Um Ayman had sent us a platter of dates and a goblet of milk and butter, which we presented to him, and he ate from it. When he finished, I stood up and poured water over the hands of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). When he washed his hands, he wiped his face and beard with the moisture of his hands. Then he went to the prayer place in the corner of the house, prayed, and fell into prostration, crying and prolonging his weeping. Then he raised his head, and none of us, the Ahl al-Bayt, dared to ask him about anything. So al-Husayn (peace be upon him) crawled until he climbed onto the thighs of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), took his head to his chest, and placed his chin on the head of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Then he said, 'O Father, what is making you cry?'

He said to him, 'O my son, I looked at you today and was pleased with you with a pleasure I had not been pleased with before like it. Then Jibril descended to me and informed me that you will be killed and that your graves will be scattered. So I praised Allah for that and asked for the best for you.' He said to him, 'O Father, then who will visit our graves and attend to them despite their scattering?' He said, 'Groups from my nation, seeking my goodness and kinship ties through that. I will attend to them on the Day of Standing and take them by their arms and save them from its terrors and hardships.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) say about who will visit the graves of the Imams in the future?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Ibn Qulawayh highlights the prophetic knowledge of the Ahl al-Bayt's future martyrdom through the revelation of Jibril, linking the emotional depth of the Prophet's weeping to the specific destiny of Imam al-Husayn. The text underscores the theological concept of 'shatat al-qubur' (scattered graves), emphasizing that despite the physical dispersion of the Imams' remains, their spiritual presence ensures that devoted visitors will be granted intercession and salvation from the terrors of the Day of Judgment.
